text.arabic_uthmani: يَٰٓأَبَتِ لَا تَعْبُدِ ٱلشَّيْطَٰنَ ۖ إِنَّ ٱلشَّيْطَٰنَ كَانَ لِلرَّحْمَٰنِ عَصِيًّۭا

words.gloss_range: direct vocative particle opening an intimate address frame
words.prose: {{ar:يا}} ({{tr:yā}}) opens the ayah by summoning the father before the prohibition arrives. The word does not add a proposition; it creates the address frame in which {{ar:أَبَتِ}} ({{tr:abati}}) is heard as the named addressee and {{ar:لَا تَعْبُدِ}} ({{tr:lā taʿbudi}}) lands as direct warning rather than detached maxim. Its lengthened opening sound lets the appeal breathe before the clipped negative command.

topics.headline: direct address before content
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the prohibition as speech to a present father, not as an abstract rule.
topics.reason: QAC identifies the word as a vocative particle, and attachment evidence binds it to the father-address that controls the following prohibition.

topics.headline: appeal softens the command
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that relational recognition precedes correction and shapes the command's tone.
topics.reason: The opening vocative and its link to the tender father-form place address before the negative jussive clause.

words.gloss_range: affective father-vocative with compressed first-person relation
words.root_gloss_range: fatherhood, origin, and family authority; disputed refusal associations remain only contrastive here
words.prose: {{ar:أَبَتِ}} ({{tr:abati}}) is not a neutral father noun. Its special vocative form compresses the speaker's own father-relation into a tender address, while the following second-person verb makes that same father responsible for the forbidden act. The word keeps the hierarchy reversal precise: a son corrects the family authority without dropping filial tenderness. Variant final-vowel evidence and the disputed root-shadow do not change that local address. It also belongs to the repeated {{ar:يَا أَبَتِ}} ({{tr:yā abati}}) appeal across the scene (19:42, 19:43, 19:45), where the earlier worship-question becomes this direct prohibition.

topics.headline: tender father-vocative form
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that the rebuke is carried by a special affectionate address, not by a cold kinship label.
topics.reason: The QAC grammar marks a vocative with affective ending, and the attachment evidence makes it the addressee of the opening call.

topics.headline: father receives the correction
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the reversal: the child warns the father while still naming him as father.
topics.reason: The father-address resolves the addressee of the following second-person prohibition, so the family authority is the one being corrected.

topics.headline: form variation preserves the address
topics.reader_payoff: The reader keeps the father-address stable while noticing that vowel and root-dispute evidence does not turn the word into refusal-language.
topics.reason: Variant vowel evidence leaves the vocative relation intact, and the local root alignment supports fatherhood rather than making refusal the local sense.

topics.headline: sustained appeal formula
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears this word as one turn in a sustained filial appeal, not as an isolated address.
topics.reason: The bundle's cross-reference and same-surah rows place the formula around this ayah, especially the move from the worship question in 19:42 to the prohibition in 19:44.

topics.headline: kinship faces allegiance
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees human kinship placed beside the larger allegiance relation involving Shayṭān and al-Raḥmān.
topics.reason: The father noun opens the human relation, while the causal clause later defines the theological relation that explains the warning.

words.gloss_range: prohibitive negative particle governing the following jussive verb

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: definite object of the prohibited verb

words.prose: {{ar:لَا}} ({{tr:lā}}) is prohibitive rather than descriptive negation. It governs {{ar:تَعْبُدِ}} ({{tr:taʿbudi}}) and makes the father's worship-service of {{ar:الشَّيْطَانَ}} ({{tr:al-shayṭāna}}) the barred domain. Structurally, it pivots from tender address into a complete command before {{ar:إِنَّ}} ({{tr:inna}}) supplies the rationale.

topics.headline: negative command, not description
topics.reader_payoff: The reader recognizes a command of non-action rather than a statement that worship is absent.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment support identify the particle as prohibitive and tie its scope to the verb-object clause.

topics.headline: prohibition precedes explanation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the ayah move from relational call to restraint before the causal explanation begins.
topics.reason: The prohibition clause is syntactically complete before the following emphatic rationale clause.

words.gloss_range: jussive Form I worship or service directed to an explicit forbidden object
words.root_gloss_range: worship, service, devotion, and slave-like submission; non-surface derived images only color the local Form I act
words.prose: {{ar:تَعْبُدِ}} ({{tr:taʿbudi}}) is the governed jussive verb of the prohibition, with the father as its second-person addressee and {{ar:الشَّيْطَانَ}} ({{tr:al-shayṭāna}}) as explicit object. The root's worship-service range makes the warning larger than ritual gesture: it bars transferring obedience, devotion, and mastery to the wrong recipient. That personal command also echoes the wider ban on serving Shayṭān (36:60) while the same scene turns the earlier question about the father's worship (19:42) into a categorical stop. Across the boundary from the guidance-following appeal in 19:43, the issue becomes where the father directs submission; false worship later turns against the worshipper (19:82).

topics.headline: direct object fixes the ban
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees a specific father-directed action barred toward a named object, not generic piety language.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence marks the following noun as the explicit object, and QAC marks the verb as jussive after the prohibitive particle.

topics.headline: service implies misdirected allegiance
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the barred worship also carries service and mastery pressure, while the local form remains simple Form I.
topics.reason: The local verb is Form I with an explicit object, so derived Form II or Form V images can color the worship-service field but cannot replace the selected local sense.

topics.headline: universal ban made personal
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the broad Quranic warning against serving Shayṭān narrowed into a son's direct plea to his father (36:60).
topics.reason: The row-supplied parallels preserve the same worship-of-Shayṭān pattern while local grammar personalizes the command.

topics.headline: wrong service versus true servitude
topics.reader_payoff: The reader connects the prohibition of serving Shayṭān with the surah's larger contrast between false service and coming to al-Raḥmān as servants (19:93).
topics.reason: The same ayah opposes giving service to Shayṭān with Shayṭān's own disobedience toward al-Raḥmān, and the supplied same-surah echoes extend that contrast.

topics.headline: act and object before reason
topics.reader_payoff: The reader tracks the ayah's sequence: tender address, complete prohibition, then theological reason.
topics.reason: The verb-object pair completes the command before the emphatic rationale clause begins.

topics.headline: following becomes service
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees continuity from the prior invitation to follow guidance into the present warning about where obedience is directed.
topics.reason: The same addressed father remains in view across the boundary, and the command tests the object of his obedience.

words.gloss_range: the definite named adversary as direct object of forbidden worship-service
words.root_gloss_range: Shayṭān as named adversary; far-removal, fiery, and loanword etymologies remain qualifying pressures rather than a replacement for the local noun
words.prose: The first {{ar:الشَّيْطَانَ}} ({{tr:al-shayṭāna}}) is the accusative object of {{ar:تَعْبُدِ}} ({{tr:taʿbudi}}), putting the named adversary in the recipient slot of service. Its definiteness presumes a known referent, while disputed etymological pressures such as far-removal, adversary, and fiery destructiveness deepen why this object is unfit for worship without changing the local noun sense. The same name then returns after {{ar:إِنَّ}} ({{tr:inna}}), so the forbidden object becomes the subject of the causal indictment. The pattern also recalls Shayṭān's defect formula in 17:27 and points forward to the father's risk of alliance with Shayṭān in 19:45.

topics.headline: Shayṭān receives the service slot
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the moral inversion: the named adversary occupies the object position of worship-service.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence marks this noun as the direct object of the worship verb, and QAC marks it as a definite concrete noun.

topics.headline: adversary images qualify the name
topics.reader_payoff: The reader gains adversary, distance, and destructive color around the named object while keeping the local sense as Shayṭān.
topics.reason: The input itself flags root uncertainty and multiple derivational analyses, so they can color the noun but cannot govern the local parse.

topics.headline: object returns as accused subject
topics.reader_payoff: The reader follows one named figure from forbidden recipient to indicted rebel without a pronoun softening the link.
topics.reason: The same definite noun appears in the prohibition and then as the governed subject of the rationale clause.

topics.headline: rebel formula points forward
topics.reader_payoff: The reader connects this named object to recurring defect formulas and to the next ayah's alliance warning (19:45).
topics.reason: The supplied parallels connect Shayṭān with characterization formulas and the next ayah reuses the referent in an alliance-risk construction.

words.gloss_range: emphatic explanatory particle introducing the rationale clause

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: repeated definite subject of the rationale clause
divine name in the directed predicate relation

words.prose: {{ar:إِنَّ}} ({{tr:inna}}) pivots the ayah from command into asserted reason. Its scope reaches through the repeated {{ar:الشَّيْطَانَ}} ({{tr:al-shayṭāna}}), the copula, the directed relation to {{ar:الرَّحْمَنِ}} ({{tr:al-raḥmāni}}), and the final predicate. By taking the full name rather than a pronoun, the particle renews the forbidden figure inside the causal claim. The clause is attached without an intervening connector, making the rationale adhere tightly to the prohibition.

topics.headline: asserted reason for the ban
topics.reader_payoff: The reader understands the second half as the stated ground of the prohibition, not as a loose comment.
topics.reason: QAC marks the particle as an assertive annulment particle, and attachment support identifies the following unit as the explanatory assertion.

topics.headline: full noun after the particle
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the causal claim renames Shayṭān instead of replacing him with a lighter pronoun.
topics.reason: The particle governs the repeated definite noun, renewing the referent in the rationale clause.

topics.headline: reason follows without delay
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the command and reason pressed together as one persuasive move.
topics.reason: The rationale begins directly after the prohibition rather than with an added coordinating particle.

words.gloss_range: repeated definite Shayṭān as governed subject of the explanatory predicate chain
words.root_gloss_range: named adversary field carried from the object clause into the causal characterization
words.prose: The second {{ar:الشَّيْطَانَ}} ({{tr:al-shayṭāna}}) repeats the full definite noun where a pronoun could have appeared. Its case is still accusative, but now because {{ar:إِنَّ}} ({{tr:inna}}) governs it; functionally it has moved from worship-object to the subject of the predicate chain. The repetition makes the logic explicit: the very one the father must not serve is the one being characterized as rebellious toward al-Raḥmān.

topics.headline: name repeated instead of pronoun
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the named adversary renewed at the hinge between prohibition and reason.
topics.reason: The noun is repeated as a full definite form after the emphatic particle rather than being pronominalized.

topics.headline: same form, new syntactic role
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that identical surface form hides a role change from object of service to subject of indictment.
topics.reason: Word 5 is accusative as direct object, while word 7 is accusative as the governed subject of the emphatic clause.

topics.headline: subject waits for verdict
topics.reader_payoff: The reader follows the repeated name through the delayed predicate until the final verdict lands.
topics.reason: The repeated subject is followed by the copula and prepositional target before the final predicate completes the claim.

topics.headline: name threads into warning
topics.reader_payoff: The reader connects the repeated name here with the next ayah's risk of becoming Shayṭān's ally (19:45).
topics.reason: The supplied same-surah rows keep Shayṭān in view beyond this rationale clause, especially in the following warning.

words.gloss_range: perfect copula assigning an established character predicate
words.root_gloss_range: being, becoming, and established predication; here copular rather than eventive

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: prepositional target of the defect relation

words.prose: {{ar:كَانَ}} ({{tr:kāna}}) turns the explanation into a being-statement about Shayṭān. It is not a new action verb here; it carries the repeated subject into a predicate chain where {{ar:لِلرَّحْمَنِ}} ({{tr:li-l-raḥmāni}}) names the directed relation and {{ar:عَصِيًّا}} ({{tr:ʿaṣiyyā}}) supplies the character verdict. The perfect copular form lets the clause sound established and characterological, joining Surah 19's wider pattern of moral portraits, especially the contrast with the negated {{ar:عَصِيًّا}} ({{tr:ʿaṣiyyā}}) at 19:14 and the Shayṭān defect formula in 17:27.

topics.headline: copula forces the final predicate
topics.reader_payoff: The reader waits for the final adjective because the copula makes the causal claim incomplete until the predicate arrives.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence treats the following phrase and adjective as the predicate content of the copular verb.

topics.headline: established being, not one event
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears Shayṭān's rebellion as established character rather than a single narrated act.
topics.reason: The perfect copula with an adjective predicate supports an established or characterological predication in this local frame.

topics.headline: service command meets being statement
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the father's forbidden action grounded in what Shayṭān is.
topics.reason: The ayah moves from a jussive action clause about the father into a copular characterization of Shayṭān.

topics.headline: character formula in a larger pattern
topics.reader_payoff: The reader connects this copular defect statement with Surah 19's character contrasts and with the Shayṭān defect formula in 17:27.
topics.reason: The source rows give concrete intra-surah and cross-surah references where the same copular characterization logic recurs.

words.gloss_range: preposition directing the rebellion relation toward al-Raḥmān

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: final defect predicate directed by the preposition

words.prose: {{ar:لِ}} ({{tr:li}}) makes the final defect relational. In {{ar:لِلرَّحْمَنِ}} ({{tr:li-l-raḥmāni}}), the preposition governs the divine name and specifies the one toward whom {{ar:عَصِيًّا}} ({{tr:ʿaṣiyyā}}) is directed. Because the predicate is rebellion, the local force is not benefit or possession but adversative direction, and the target is heard before the final adjective lands.

topics.headline: rebellion aimed toward a target
topics.reader_payoff: The reader understands the disobedience as directed toward al-Raḥmān, not as an isolated trait.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence links the prepositional phrase to the final adjective, and the predicate semantics block a beneficiary reading.

topics.headline: preposition fuses with the name
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices relation and target compressed into one heard unit before the verdict.
topics.reason: The preposition governs the following genitive divine name and forms the fused surface phrase.

topics.headline: target precedes the final label
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears whom Shayṭān defies before hearing the final word that names him rebellious.
topics.reason: The phrase can be described in the copular predicate environment or as complementing the adjective, but either way it directs the defect toward al-Raḥmān before the adjective closes the clause.

words.gloss_range: the proper divine mercy-name as the directed target of Shayṭān's rebellion
words.root_gloss_range: mercy, comprehensive mercy, and generative compassion; non-surface reciprocal or womb imagery remains qualifying pressure

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: prepositional phrase naming the target of rebellion

words.prose: {{ar:الرَّحْمَنِ}} ({{tr:al-raḥmāni}}) is the governed divine name inside {{ar:لِلرَّحْمَنِ}} ({{tr:li-l-raḥmāni}}), placed before the final defect predicate. The ayah names al-Raḥmān rather than a generic divine title, so Shayṭān's rebellion is framed as defiance of comprehensive mercy; the root field of mercy as bestowal and generative compassion intensifies the paradox without replacing the proper-name function. Same-surah echoes make that choice heavier: the name recurs densely in Surah 19, the next ayah fears punishment from al-Raḥmān (19:45), the servants of al-Raḥmān stand as the opposite pole in 25:63, and the surah later says all come to al-Raḥmān as servants (19:93).

topics.headline: rebellion targets the mercy-name
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that the target of rebellion is not generic authority but the comprehensive mercy-name.
topics.reason: QAC marks the word as a proper divine name governed by the preposition, and the CRITICAL rows tie the chosen name to the final predicate.

topics.headline: root imagery colors the name
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels mercy as bestowal and generative compassion while keeping the local word as the proper name al-Raḥmān.
topics.reason: Root-family images and non-surface forms can qualify the selected name but do not replace the local proper-name function.

topics.headline: target before verdict
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the one defied before the final word declares Shayṭān rebellious.
topics.reason: The prepositional phrase precedes the final adjective and is syntactically tied to the directed rebellion relation.

topics.headline: Surah 19 mercy-name thread
topics.reader_payoff: The reader connects this target of rebellion to the surah's repeated al-Raḥmān thread and the immediate consequence warning (19:45).
topics.reason: The source rows provide concrete same-surah references where al-Raḥmān frames refuge, consequence, and universal return.

topics.headline: servants of mercy versus rebel
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees Shayṭān's directed rebellion set against the wider pattern of servants belonging to al-Raḥmān (25:63; 19:93).
topics.reason: The retained parallels explicitly oppose service to al-Raḥmān with Shayṭān's rebellion toward al-Raḥmān.

words.gloss_range: indefinite accusative qualitative predicate: rebellious, willfully disobedient
words.root_gloss_range: disobedience, non-compliance, rebellion; staff-root authority imagery remains disputed and secondary
words.prose: {{ar:عَصِيًّا}} ({{tr:ʿaṣiyyā}}) is the final predicate of {{ar:كَانَ}} ({{tr:kāna}}), not an object or loose circumstance. Its indefinite qualitative form characterizes Shayṭān as willfully rebellious toward al-Raḥmān, and its final position lets that verdict close the ayah as the reason the father must not serve him. A disputed staff-root pressure can make resistance to authority faintly felt, but it remains secondary to the surface sense of disobedience. The rare form also sharpens Surah 19's contrast: Yaḥyā is negated as {{ar:عَصِيًّا}} ({{tr:ʿaṣiyyā}}) at 19:14, while Shayṭān is affirmed as such here, with related breach formulas in 2:61 and 3:112. Its doubled sound and tanwīn cadence give the closing verdict audible weight without changing the grammar.

topics.headline: final word is the predicate
topics.reader_payoff: The reader assigns the final adjective to Shayṭān as predicate, not to al-Raḥmān or to an object slot.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence identifies the word as the accusative predicate of the copula and routes it back to the Shayṭān subject.

topics.headline: deep-seated rebellion
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears deliberate non-compliance as a character quality, not ignorance or a momentary lapse.
topics.reason: The qualitative adjective form and supplied semantics support willful disobedience as durable characterization.

topics.headline: authority-resistance image remains secondary
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can sense an authority-resistance image while keeping the surface meaning as disobedient.
topics.reason: The row itself marks the staff relation as disputed, so it survives only as latent pressure and does not govern the local adjective.

topics.headline: non-service explains false service
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees why serving Shayṭān is incoherent: he is defined by refusal of service toward al-Raḥmān.
topics.reason: The first clause concerns worship-service, while the final predicate supplies the opposite moral quality in the rationale clause.

topics.headline: verdict closes the ayah
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the ayah withhold the moral label until the final sound and final word.
topics.reason: The final predicate comes only after address, prohibition, emphatic subject, copula, and directed target.

topics.headline: rare adjective forms a moral contrast
topics.reader_payoff: The reader connects this affirmed rebellion with the rare negated use for Yaḥyā at 19:14 and with wider breach formulas (2:61; 3:112).
topics.reason: The source rows give concrete references where the same adjective or related root participates in moral-contrast formulas.

topics.headline: heavy closing cadence
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the final predicate's doubled sound and tanwīn cadence reinforce the weight of the verdict without changing its grammar.
topics.reason: The prosodic rows are locally tied to the final predicate form and its clause-ending position.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Explicitly commands humanity not to worship Satan, making it the closest verbal and thematic parallel.

inter_ayah_rows.label: no value
inter_ayah_rows.note: A declaration of faith does not clarify Satanic worship, rebellion, or Ibrahim's warning.

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak
inter_ayah_rows.note: God's mercy provides a broad backdrop to the divine name in the focus ayah, without addressing Satan or worship.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: The next verse continues Ibrahim's address to his father, warning that he may become Satan's ally through punishment from the Most Merciful.

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak
inter_ayah_rows.note: The Merciful Lord's greeting of peace only generally resonates with the divine name in the focus ayah.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: The repeated names of the Most Merciful and Merciful illuminate the divine name against which Satan is described as rebellious.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: Identifies Satan as humanity's clear enemy and as a source of discord, supporting Ibrahim's warning against serving him.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: The father's hostile reply is the immediate narrative consequence of Ibrahim's warning against his worship.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Ibrahim says idols have led many astray and contrasts following him with disobeying him, closely extending the focus warning.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: Uses the title the Most Merciful within a dispute over proper worship, though its immediate argument differs.

inter_ayah_rows.label: no value
inter_ayah_rows.note: Solomon's horses do not clarify Satanic worship or rebellion toward the Most Merciful.

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak
inter_ayah_rows.note: A promise not to disobey a teacher is only a general contrast to Satan's rebellion.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: Names Satan's allies and contrasts their cause with God's, supporting the focus ayah's warning about allegiance.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: God's mercy granted to Ibrahim follows the conflict with his father, continuing the local narrative at a distance.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: Noah's command to worship God alone and warning of punishment closely parallels the prophetic corrective form of the focus ayah.

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak
inter_ayah_rows.note: The attribution of a child to the Most Merciful concerns the same divine name but not Satanic worship.

inter_ayah_rows.label: no value
inter_ayah_rows.note: Satanic labor under Solomon does not bear on worshiping Satan or his rebellion.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: Satanic incitement of disbelievers helps explain the corrupting influence Ibrahim warns his father to reject.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Ibrahim's preceding question exposes his father's idols as powerless, directly grounding the warning not to serve Satan.

inter_ayah_rows.label: no value
inter_ayah_rows.note: Submission to Solomon does not clarify worship of Satan or the Most Merciful.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: Jacob warns his son of Satan's clear enmity, reinforcing the focus ayah's portrayal of Satan as a danger.

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak
inter_ayah_rows.note: A denial that the Most Merciful takes a child uses the same divine name but does not explain the warning.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Ibrahim's peaceful response and promise of prayer show the filial concern that governs his preceding warning.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: Rejects powerless gods besides the Most Merciful, supporting the monotheistic alternative to serving Satan.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Previous worship obstructs the queen from guidance, a close parallel to Ibrahim's concern about his father's idolatry.

inter_ayah_rows.label: no value
inter_ayah_rows.note: Idris's exaltation does not clarify the focus ayah.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: Links denial with disobedience, providing a general counterpart to Satan's rebelliousness.

inter_ayah_rows.label: no value
inter_ayah_rows.note: The Most Merciful's true kingship on Judgment Day is too general to explain Satanic service.

inter_ayah_rows.label: no value
inter_ayah_rows.note: The elevation of the Prophet's remembrance is unrelated to the focus warning.

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak
inter_ayah_rows.note: Disobeying a leader by failing to follow him is a distant formal parallel to rebellion.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: John's goodness to his parents and lack of rebellion contrast with the father's rejection and Satan's rebelliousness.

inter_ayah_rows.label: no value
inter_ayah_rows.note: Destruction of stronger towns does not clarify the focus ayah.

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak
inter_ayah_rows.note: Disobeying God and His messenger has consequences, but the verse lacks the focus's Satanic-worship relation.

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak
inter_ayah_rows.note: Joseph attributes family estrangement to Satan, offering a distant family-context parallel.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: Commands knowledge of God's oneness, the essential theological alternative to serving Satan through idolatry.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Withdrawal from people and what they worship besides God, followed by mercy, closely parallels rejecting wrongful worship.

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak
inter_ayah_rows.note: Following the caller before the Most Merciful is a distant obedience contrast, not a warning about Satan.

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak
inter_ayah_rows.note: A community's threat to stone messengers resembles the father's later threat but does not clarify the focus itself.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Commands God's servants to worship Him alone, directly supplying the positive alternative to serving Satan.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Rejects inherited worship as following a call ultimately leading from Satan, directly illuminating Ibrahim's appeal to his father.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: Calls Satan rebellious, directly echoing the focus description, though in a different setting.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: Joins worshipers with what they worship, helping frame the relational nature of the father's idolatry.

inter_ayah_rows.label: no value
inter_ayah_rows.note: A daughter's advice to her father about hiring does not clarify the focus ayah.

inter_ayah_rows.label: no value
inter_ayah_rows.note: Passing by ruined towns offers no relevant connection.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: Fear of disobeying the Lord provides a direct ethical contrast to Satan's rebellion toward the Most Merciful.

inter_ayah_rows.label: no value
inter_ayah_rows.note: Unbelief in God is too general without a link to Satan, worship, or Ibrahim's address.

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak
inter_ayah_rows.note: Job's suffering attributed to Satan is only a general Satan reference with a different function.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: States that jinn and humans were created to worship God, directly contrasting proper worship with serving Satan.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: Pharaoh's prior rebellion shows the seriousness of persistent disobedience, though without the focus's worship relation.

inter_ayah_rows.label: no value
inter_ayah_rows.note: A description of Paradise wine is unrelated.

inter_ayah_rows.label: no value
inter_ayah_rows.note: Marriage prohibitions and God's mercy do not clarify the focus ayah.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: A son respectfully tells his father to obey God's command, a meaningful filial-obedience contrast.

inter_ayah_rows.label: no value
inter_ayah_rows.note: Submission on Judgment Day does not add a specific connection.

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak
inter_ayah_rows.note: Seeking forgiveness from the Merciful God is only an attribute-level parallel.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: A prophet refuses to disobey God after receiving proof and mercy, paralleling the focus's opposition to rebellion.

inter_ayah_rows.label: no value
inter_ayah_rows.note: The greeting to Noah does not clarify the focus ayah.

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak
inter_ayah_rows.note: Repentance and divine mercy are relevant only as a broad remedy for disobedience.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: A covenant rejects associating partners with God and commands obedience, supporting the positive alternative to idolatrous service.

inter_ayah_rows.label: no value
inter_ayah_rows.note: The greeting to Moses and Aaron has no material connection.

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak
inter_ayah_rows.note: The youths ask for mercy and right guidance, but not in relation to Satanic worship.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Calls Satan ungrateful toward his Lord, closely paralleling the focus ayah's description of his rebellion toward the Most Merciful.

inter_ayah_rows.label: no value
inter_ayah_rows.note: The greeting to Elias is unrelated.

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak
inter_ayah_rows.note: Divine forgiveness and mercy are too general to clarify Satan's rebellion.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Satan leads a person away from remembrance and then abandons him, directly explaining the danger Ibrahim names.

inter_ayah_rows.label: no value
inter_ayah_rows.note: The greeting to Abraham alone does not develop the focus warning.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium

facets.statement: Bir başkasının durumu karşısında yüreğin yumuşaması, ona acıma ve içten yakınlık duyma çekirdeği oluşturur.
Bu iç yöneliş, acınan kişiyi esirgemeyi ve ona iyilikte bulunmayı gerektiren etkin bir sonuç taşır.
Topluluğun bireylerinin birbirine acıyıp birbirini esirgemesi, çekirdeğin karşılıklı bir kuruluşta gerçekleşmesidir.
Bir kimsenin Tanrı'nın esirgemesine erişmesini dilemek, çekirdek anlamdan doğan kalıplaşmış bir söz eylemidir.
Tanrı hakkında kullanıldığında esirgemenin genişliği ve yaratılmışlara iyilik olarak ulaşması belirginleşir.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Her türlü buyruk tutmama durumunu kapsar; büyüklük taslama veya sınırı aşma koşulu aramaz.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Büyüklük taslayarak boyun eğmeme, diklenme ve bu yolla sınırı aşma özelliklerini taşır.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: İki dal da kendisinden söz dinlemesi beklenen kişinin boyun eğmemesini ve buyruktan çıkmasını içerir.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak dalda yalın buyruk tutmama yeterlidir. Komşu dal ise bu davranışı büyüklük taslama, diklenme veya ölçüyü aşma biçimiyle sınırlar; bu yüzden her örnekte birbirlerinin yerine geçmezler.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Karşı gelmeyi özellikle buyruk verme ve söz dinleme bağı içinde kurar.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Buyruk ilişkisi bulunmadan da karşı karşıya gelme, engel olma, çekişme ve çatışmayı kapsar.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Bir kişinin kendisinden beklenen tutuma aykırı davranıp karşı koyduğu durumlarda iki dal örtüşebilir.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak dalın belirleyici ölçütü, uyulması beklenen bir buyruğun tutulmamasıdır. Komşu dalın karşıtlığı daha geniştir ve eşit konumdaki kişiler arasında ya da herhangi bir buyruk olmadan da kurulabilir.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Buyruğu tutmama, karşı gelme ve beklenen boyun eğmeden çıkma kutbunu bildirir.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Söz dinleme ve boyun eğmenin yanı sıra benimsenen yol ve kulluk düzeni gibi daha geniş alanlara uzanır.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: İki dal, buyruk veren ile ona uyması beklenen kişi arasındaki söz dinleme eksenini paylaşır.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak dal bu eksenin uymama kutbudur; komşu dal ise uyma ve boyun eğme kutbudur. Komşunun daha geniş düzen ve benimsenen yol anlamları, bu karşıtlığın dışında kalır.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Buyruğa uymayan kişinin söz dinleme yükümlülüğünü çiğnemesini merkez alır.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Kişiden uzaklaşma, soğuk davranma, bağını kesme veya istenen şeyi vermeme gibi daha geniş kopuşları kapsar.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Birinden uzaklaşmanın onun sözünü dinlememe biçiminde gerçekleştiği durumlarda anlam alanları kesişir.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak dal için buyruk ve ona uymama bağı zorunludur. Komşu dalda ayrılma, soğukluk veya vermeme bulunabilir; bunlar bir buyruğa karşı gelmeyi gerektirmez.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Doğru yol üzerine bir yargı kurmadan, verilmiş buyruğu tutmamayı anlatır.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Doğru olandan sapma, bilinen gerçeği geri çevirme, ölçüyü aşma ve inatla direnme özelliklerini kapsar.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Bir buyruğa uymama, doğru olduğu bilinen şeye karşı direnme biçimini aldığında iki dal aynı olaya uygulanabilir.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak dalda buyruğa uymamak yeterlidir ve buyruğun doğruluğu hakkında yargı gerekmez. Komşu dal, doğruya ya da düzgün yola aykırılığı ve çoğu kez direnme veya sınırı aşma yönünü öne çıkarır.

branches.neighbor_coverage_note: Sekiz adayın tamamı değerlendirildi. Buyruk verme, kişiler arasında barışı kurma ve ayrışanları uzlaştırma dalları yalnız aynı olay alanına uzaktan dokunduğu, bağımsız bir anlam yakınlığı ya da ortak karşıtlık ekseni kurmadığı için ayrım listesine alınmadı.
branches.what_is_ar: يدخل فيه عصى فلان أميره أو ربه، والعصيان والمعصية، واستعصت الجماعة إذا خرجت عن طاعة السلطان.
branches.what_is_not_ar: لا يدخل فيه معنى العصا نفسها، ولا الضرب بها، ولا التوكؤ عليها، ولا صلابة النواة أو عرق لا يرقأ؛ وألفاظ شق العصا وإلقاء العصا ولين العصا من مادة العصا المجاورة إلا حيث يصرح المصدر بعلاقة الخروج عن الجماعة.
branches.source_phrase_ar: العصيان خلاف الطاعة، وقد عصاه يعصيه عصيا ومعصية (sihah)؛ عصى فلان أميره يعصيه عصيا وعصيانا إذا لم يطعه، وعصى العبد ربه إذا خالف أمره (tahdhib)؛ عصى عصيانا إذا خرج عن الطاعة (mufradat)
